subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Machine Vision: Robots That See
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Machine Vision: Robots That See.

hook.text: A camera watches the conveyor belt. Software finds the part, measures its position, and tells the robot where to grab.

buildup.text: 2D vision identifies shapes and positions in a flat image. It works well for objects lying flat on a surface.

discovery.text: 3D vision adds depth perception. Structured light or stereo cameras let robots pick randomly heaped parts from a bin.

twist.text: Lighting is the hardest part. Shiny metal reflects glare, dark rubber absorbs light. Bad lighting blinds the camera.

climax.text: Deep learning now identifies objects that traditional algorithms can't handle. Robots recognize parts they've never seen before.

punchline.text: Give a robot eyes and it stops needing perfect order. It adapts.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge in industrial machine vision?
options: Cameras are too slow to capture fast-moving conveyor belt items
Lighting conditions must be carefully controlled to avoid glare and shadows
Robots cannot process camera data fast enough for real-time decisions
